patent_grounding.rationale: The modeled chuck, translating jaws, internal torque-transfer train, motor/receiver drive member, workpiece, and automation handler are supported by the supplied claim and embodiment passages. The separate torque coupling and receiver mounting relation are consistent with claim 14; the motor-receiver structural association is a reasonable representation of the receiver including its drive member. Replacement steps match claim 14, and the model avoids inferring an unsupported feedback controller.

functional_completeness.rationale: The key disclosed path from motor torque through the chuck transmission to jaws and clamping contact is represented, as is the automated chuck replacement behavior. No significant supported function needed for this abstraction is omitted.

flow_consistency.rationale: Torque, jaw-drive rotation, clamping force, and structural mounting/handling are distinguished by descriptive compatible flow types. The motor-to-transmission interface is correctly separate from the chuck-to-receiver mounting interface. Port direction choices are compatible with the represented bidirectional structural contacts.

claim_traceability.rationale: Major system elements and behaviors trace to cited claims or embodiment passages. The modeled motor option and robot/automation handling remain within the patent's disclosed options; unspecified sensing/control details are not asserted.

interfaces.rationale: The earlier gaps are addressed: MOTOR has a structural association with DRIVE, and HANDLER has explicit structural handling interactions with CHUCK and DRIVE. The torque coupling remains separately modeled. Reuse of CHUCK.receiver_mount and DRIVE.chuck_mount for replacement handling and receiver mounting is semantically understandable and not an incompatible flow.

textbook_application.rationale: Retrieved guidance supports separating the system from relevant external actors and representing physical/functional interactions. It is applied as modeling guidance only, not as evidence of invention facts.

summary: Revision 15 addresses the prior interface and connectivity concerns without disturbing the grounded torque path. The SJS is coherent and patent-supported at this abstraction; I found no actionable unresolved issues.
